metaData.title: Building Reliable Agentic AI Systems
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article presents a detailed case study of Bayer's PRINCE platform, an agentic AI system built on Agentic RAG that transforms complex preclinical data retrieval into an intuitive conversational experience, with a focus on the engineering decisions behind its reliable architecture.
metaData.summary: This article is a comprehensive case study from Bayer, detailing the engineering journey behind PRINCE (Preclinical Information Center), an agentic AI system designed to revolutionize preclinical drug discovery data access. The article begins by outlining the challenge: navigating a maze of siloed, structured and unstructured data (PDF reports, study metadata) using traditional keyword search. It then introduces PRINCE's evolutionary path from a 'Search' tool to an 'Ask' system using RAG, and finally to a 'Do' platform with multi-agent orchestration. The core of the article is a deep dive into the system's architecture, built on LangGraph and FastAPI. It explains the key engineering concepts of 'context engineering' (providing different context to different agents) and 'harness engineering' (scaffolding around LLMs). The article details the agentic workflow, including steps for clarifying user intent, a dedicated 'Think & Plan' step for process reflection, and the roles of Researcher, Writer, and Reflection agents. It provides a thorough breakdown of the hybrid retrieval strategy, combining RAG for unstructured data (with a detailed query-time pipeline including keyword extraction, metadata filtering, query expansion, hybrid search, and reranking) and Text-to-SQL for structured data. The article also covers resilience, error handling, and observability, emphasizing the importance of fallbacks and continuous evaluation. It concludes by discussing the evolution towards domain-specific sub-agents to manage complexity as the system scales.

mainPoints.point: Reliable agentic AI requires disciplined context engineering, not just larger context windows.
mainPoints.explanation: The article argues that providing different, focused context to each agent stage (planning, retrieval, reflection, writing) reduces context pollution, improves steerability, and makes the system easier to debug and evaluate.

mainPoints.point: A dedicated 'Think & Plan' step for process reflection is critical for multi-step agentic workflows.
mainPoints.explanation: This step allows the system to reason about its strategy, evaluate tool selection, and assess progress towards the goal before taking action, leading to dramatic improvements in accuracy for complex queries.

mainPoints.point: A hybrid retrieval strategy combining RAG and Text-to-SQL is essential for bridging unstructured and structured enterprise data.
mainPoints.explanation: RAG excels at extracting insights from narrative reports (PDFs), while Text-to-SQL is better for precise filtering and aggregation of structured data, and the system intelligently routes queries to the appropriate tool.

mainPoints.point: Evolving towards a hierarchy of domain-specific sub-agents is key to managing complexity at scale.
mainPoints.explanation: As the system expands across multiple domains, a single agent with a flat tool list becomes unmanageable. Domain-specific sub-agents with their own tools and prompts keep responsibilities coherent and prevent cross-domain leakage.

keyQuotes: Larger context windows did not remove the need to be selective about what each agent sees. In early iterations, putting too much information into the context made the system harder to steer and harder to evaluate.
The 'Think & Plan' step provides this metacognitive capability, allowing the system to reflect on its own workflow and adjust its strategy accordingly.
This 'fail-fast' mechanism prevents wasted execution on vague queries, while careful tuning ensures the system remains unobtrusive when the intent is already clear.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5, a generally available Mythos-class model with state-of-the-art capabilities, alongside Claude Mythos 5 for trusted cybersecurity partners, with new safeguards to mitigate misuse risks.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI Introduces GPT-5.5: A New Class of Intelligence for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI announces GPT-5.5, a new model designed for complex goal understanding and autonomous task completion, now available in ChatGPT and Codex.

relatedArticles.title: Codex Now Integrates Directly with Chrome on macOS and Windows
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces a new Chrome extension for Codex on macOS and Windows, enabling the AI to operate directly within a user's live browser session to perform complex, parallel automation tasks using their active profile and direct code execution.

relatedArticles.title: Feedback Flywheel
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Martin Fowler proposes a 'Feedback Flywheel' for AI-assisted development, transforming individual intuition into shared team infrastructure through lightweight rituals and artifact updates.

relatedArticles.title: Structured-Prompt-Driven Development (SPDD)
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Structured Prompt-Driven Development (SPDD) is an engineering method that treats prompts as first-class delivery artifacts, enabling teams to govern, review, and reuse AI-generated code at scale.

relatedArticles.title: Andrej Karpathy on Code Agents， AutoResearch， and the Loopy Era of AI
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Andrej Karpathy explores the paradigm shift from manual programming to agent orchestration, the automation of AI research, and the profound implications for software engineering and education.

relatedArticles.title: What Is Code?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Code is not just instructions for machines but a conceptual model of a problem domain, and as LLMs commoditize code generation, building precise vocabulary and shared understanding becomes the developer's core value.

relatedArticles.title: Introducing workspace agents in ChatGPT
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI introduces workspace agents, a new class of shared, long-running AI agents within ChatGPT for business teams, designed to automate complex workflows, integrate with organizational tools, and operate under enterprise-grade controls.

relatedArticles.title: Harness engineering for coding agent users
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Martin Fowler defines 'harness engineering' as the systematic practice of building feedforward guides and feedback sensors to steer AI coding agents toward maintainable, architecturally fit, and functionally correct code.

relatedArticles.title: Maintainability sensors for coding agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores how static code analysis sensors, enhanced with custom guidance for AI coding agents, can help maintain codebase maintainability by providing fast feedback and enabling agent self-correction.
